• Name: Ear snail (also European ear snail, Pokemon snail)
  • Water type: freshwater/brackish
  • Size: 2 – 2.5 cm
  • Temperature: 18 – 30°C
  • pH: 7.0 – 8.0
  • GH: 8 – 30; KH: 4 – 16
  • Nitrate: less than 80 ppm
  • Diet: algae eater/detritivore
  • Temperament: peaceful
  • Life span: up to 1 year
  • Colour: pale yellow to dark brown

Radix rubiginosa is native to Indonesia, Vietnam and Indo-China. However, it has proven highly invasive because of its wide environmental tolerances. Through the pet and aquarium trade, particularly aquarium plants, it is gradually expanding its range and displacing local fauna.

It can be found in Taiwan, China, Japan, Australia, Russia (Lake Baikal), the USA and South Africa. It is also listed as a "hothouse" alien species in Great Britain, Ireland and Israel.
Ear snails inhabit a wide variety of freshwater habitats such as lakes, ponds, swamps, marshes, rice fields, small canals and ditches. They generally prefer stagnant or slow-moving water.
Tank size does not matter for these snails. They can live in basically any nano tank.

Temperature: this species tolerates gradual decreases down to 10°C, but activity drops noticeably. The ideal range is 18 – 30°C.

pH: found in both alkaline and acidic waters, but the optimum is 7.0 – 8.0. If pH stays below 6.0 for weeks or months, shell formation may suffer, as calcium uptake becomes difficult.

Hardness: they prefer hard water, KH > 4 and GH > 8.

Filtration: no special requirements. To breed them as live food and boost numbers, a basic sponge filter can be used.

Lighting: no special requirements; adapt it to the plants (and/or algae).

Substrate: any substrate works, but smooth gravel is recommended since algae grow on it more easily and these snails do not usually burrow.

These snails are omnivorous and great scavengers. In aquariums they graze mainly on biofilm and algae, including diatoms, green spot algae and green dust algae. They also eat blanched vegetables such as carrot, spinach, cucumber and zucchini.

They are safe in planted tanks: they feed on algae and decaying plant matter and usually do not eat healthy live plants.

These snails are nocturnal and often hide and rest during the day. They are peaceful, non-aggressive, solitary and very shy, and prefer calm water and peaceful tank mates.

They do not dig and can float by filling the cavity with air. They climb on plants, rocks and driftwood, so be careful if the water level is very high.

These snails are hermaphrodites and can potentially self-fertilize, although cross-mating is more common.

  • They mature at about 2 months old.
  • Eggs are laid in transparent capsules of 10-20 eggs; the largest had 134 eggs.
  • Incubation lasts 12 days at 10°C, 8 days at 25°C and 6 days at 30°C; hatching success is highest at 25°C.
  • Fecundity peaks at 10 weeks (128 eggs per snail).
  • Young hatch as crawling juveniles.

They are excellent food for assassin snails, crayfish, loaches, pufferfish and oscars, and thrive in any community tank.

Do not collect these snails from the wild: Lymnaeidae can be intermediate hosts of trematodes (Fasciola spp.) and nematodes (Angiostrongylus malaysiensis) that infect humans or livestock.

Once established, they are hard to get rid of because they are hardy and prolific.
